Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Ghana Maritime Authority moves to operationalise 12-nautical-mile fishing exclusion zone to protect artisanal fishers Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 24 November 2026 6:39pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) has begun steps to update the country's official maritime charts to reflect the boundaries of the 12-nautical-mile Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ), as part of efforts to strengthen enforcement and protect artisanal fishing activities along the coast.
The move was announced following a multi-stakeholder dialogue organised by the GMA with support from Oceana Ghana to address outstanding technical and administrative requirements for the full implementation of the protected zone.
The Authority said it had initiated the chart update process following a request from the Fisheries Commission, to ensure that the designated boundaries are formally recognised by all users of Ghana's maritime space.
The engagement brought together government regulators, security agencies, industrial trawler operators, artisanal fishers and civil society organisations to assess progress, clarify institutional responsibilities and identify the remaining steps towards effective protection of coastal fishing waters.
The GMA also stressed the need for stronger coordination among regulatory and enforcement agencies responsible for monitoring activities within Ghana's waters.
The dialogue formed part of Oceana Ghana's Make The EEZ Real campaign, which supports state institutions in translating legal protections into practical safeguards for fishing communities.
Although the responsibility for operationalising and enforcing the zone rests primarily with government authorities, Oceana's support is intended to complement institutional efforts through transparency, public awareness and coordinated action.
Representatives of the GMA, the Ministry for Fisheries and Aquaculture, the Fisheries Commission, the Environmental Protection Agency, the Minerals Commission, the Petroleum Commission and relevant maritime security and enforcement agencies participated in the engagement.
Other participants included the National Fisheries Association of Ghana (NAFAG), the Ghana Industrial Trawlers Association, canoe owners, artisanal fishers, fish processors, civil society organisations and development partners.
The 12-nautical-mile exclusion zone was established under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), enacted in August 2025 to provide a stronger legislative framework for the sustainable management of Ghana's marine resources.
On December 29, 2025, the Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture issued Gazette Notification No. 414, officially designating all waters within the 12-nautical-mile limit, approximately 22 kilometres, as the Inshore Exclusion Zone.
The zone is reserved exclusively for small-scale artisanal fishers and canoe operators, with industrial trawler vessels prohibited from fishing within the designated waters.
The restriction is intended to keep large commercial fishing vessels away from near-shore breeding and nursery grounds, protect fragile marine habitats and allow depleted fish stocks to replenish.
It is also expected to reduce fatal collisions between industrial trawlers and wooden fishing canoes, as well as damage to fishing equipment.
However, the GMA says the legal designation alone is insufficient to guarantee protection, noting that further technical and administrative processes, alongside effective collaboration among relevant stakeholders, must be completed to translate the policy into tangible protection at sea.
